subject: Scoping: Skylab pilot — metered split + billing options
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@skylab.ai>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@skylab.ai
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Skylab pilot — meter-split proposal and billing questions

Hi Hiro,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Skylab liked the latency profile and the KV cache behaviour. We want to move forward with a 6-week POC but have two asks on packaging that will determine timing:

1) Metered split: we prefer a hybrid billing approach where base hours are reserved (flat) and overage is metered at a reduced per-token rate. Can you provide a clean matrix that shows effective CPM/token at different utilization bands?

2) Scoped deliverables vs price: our procurement wants line items for engineering hours, model tuning, and dedicated pool costs separate from the API consumption line so they can route approvals.

Attached is a rough internal cost table — can you review and propose a commercial structure?

Thanks,
Oliver
VP Product
Skylab AI

Attachments: Skylab_internal_costs.xlsx (referenced)
From: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@skylab.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skylab pilot — meter-split proposal and billing questions

Hi Oliver — thanks for the notes and the table. Laura and I reviewed this morning. High-level thoughts below; I'll follow up with a pricing workbook and a short SOW draft.

Quick answers:
- We can do a 6-week POC with a blended approach: a small reserved capacity (weekdays 9–5 expected traffic) + metered consumption outside the bucket. The reserved block is cheaper per-token at expected CPU-bound loads.
- We normally separate: Dedicated pool fee, engineering hours (time and materials), and API consumption. We can present these as separate line items for procurement and then show a single "bundled" option for exec approval.

Options to consider (we'll include numbers in the workbook):
- Option A: 40-hour reserved block + metered overage at 0.6x standard payg rate (good for bursts)
- Option B: 80-hour reserved block + lower overage at 0.45x rate, plus a 10% discount on engineering hours if Skylab commits to an enterprise trial conversion within 90 days
- Option C: Pure metered with a capped monthly spend (safety cap) — simplest procurement path but higher unit cost

Can you confirm Skylab's likely peak concurrency window and whether the engineering hours should be invoiced upfront or as a milestone? That will change the cashflow and discounting assumptions.

I'll attach a quick workbook (Skylab_POCTieredRates_v2.xlsx) and a short mutual action plan to this thread by EOD.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none in this message (workbook to follow)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@skylab.ai>, hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Skylab pilot — meter-split proposal and billing questions

Hi Oliver — looping in procurement questions and a couple legal-commercial constraints so we're clear before we finalize numbers: 

- Discounting guardrails: we can offer an engineering-hours discount tied to conversion, but any multi-line discounts need a clear trigger (signed enterprise order or usage threshold) to avoid retroactive claims.
- Invoicing cadence: Redwood prefers engineering hours invoiced on milestone completion; procurement prepayment can be accepted but will factor into the effective discount.
- SLA / support window: for a Dedicated pool we can commit to a 99.5% availability SLA during the reserved hours; out-of-scope support during the metered bursts would be handled via ticketing unless you upgrade to a premium support pack.

Ask from Skylab procurement: would the POC SOW list deliverables as timeboxed outcomes (e.g., integration complete, latency test pass, model tuning checkpoint) or as a list of effort hours? If you prefer outcomes, we can price a risk-share model instead of pure T&M.

Quick internal note: Laura, please include the escrow and billing GL lines in the workbook (procurement asked for separate line items).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

1) Peak concurrency: our internal telemetry shows peak inference traffic 11:00–14:00 PT weekdays, plus a smaller evening batch at 20:00–22:00 PT for batch re-runs. Expect 3x baseline during the midday window.
2) Engineering hours: procurement would prefer milestone invoicing tied to deliverables (makes approvals easier). We're open to the risk-share outcome model if Redwood can show a ~20% upside on conversion to justify it.

Decision request: can you send the workbook and a 1-page SOW with two billing options (milestone T&M + risk-share outcome) by EOD Friday 17 Sep? If procurement gets that, we can fast-track the PO and sign within a week.

I'll await the workbook and the MOP (mutual action plan).

Oliver
